description: PII-in-logs and worker/webhook reliability hardening (small, targeted). Mask or remove sensitive data (emails, tokens, URLs with query secrets) from log output and fix two fire-and-forget/staleness reliability nits. Addresses #1292 (email in bulk-email failure log), #1294 (stale WhatsApp access token), #1295 (Telegram fire-and-forget sendReply), #1297 (user email sent to Telegram chat). NOTE: #1293 is CLOSED — skip it. Issue line numbers are stale; locate the actual code by content, not line number.
steps: #1292 worker.ts bulk-email failure log: Find the bulk-email worker catch/failure log that includes a recipient email address in the message. Mask the email before logging (e.g. a maskEmail helper that keeps first char + domain, like `j***@example.com`) or drop the address entirely and log a non-PII identifier (recipientId/jobId). If a masking helper already exists in lib/ (grep for mask/redact/scrub, and check sentry-pii-scrub.ts), reuse it; otherwise add a tiny helper.

#1297 telegram bot: Find where a user's email is put into a Telegram chat reply/message (the line number in the issue is stale — search app/api/webhooks/telegram/bot/route.ts for the email being interpolated into sendReply text). Remove the email from the outbound Telegram message or replace it with a non-identifying reference (e.g. 'your account'), since Telegram servers may log it.

#1295 telegram fire-and-forget: In app/api/webhooks/telegram/bot/route.ts, sendReply calls fetch without await, so Telegram rate-limits cause silent failures. Make the relevant sendReply calls awaited (or collect and await them) so failures are observable/logged, without blocking the webhook 200 response longer than necessary. Ensure the webhook still returns promptly; log send failures via the project's error logger rather than swallowing.

#1294 stale WhatsApp token: In worker.ts where the WhatsApp access token is read from integration config before sending, add an expiry/staleness check or at least detect a 401/expired-token response and log a clear, actionable structured error (via logError) instead of failing silently. If token refresh infrastructure exists, prefer surfacing the staleness; do not implement a full OAuth refresh flow if none exists — document that as a follow-up.
Verify no email addresses, access tokens, or secret-bearing URLs are emitted in plaintext by the touched log statements (grep the changed lines).
acceptance_criteria: The bulk-email worker failure log no longer emits an unmasked recipient email (#1292).
The Telegram bot no longer sends the user's raw email into a Telegram chat message (#1297).
Telegram sendReply failures are awaited/observable rather than fire-and-forget-silent, while the webhook still responds promptly (#1295).
Stale/expired WhatsApp access tokens produce a clear structured log/error rather than a silent failure (#1294).
#1293 was intentionally skipped (closed) and this is noted in findings.
npm run typecheck and npm run lint pass; if worker/webhook unit tests exist they still pass.
findings:
#1292 (worker.ts bulk-email): the failure-path console.error already masked the recipient via redactEmail(). Extended the fix so the per-recipient result objects that BullMQ persists in Redis (the processor return value) also store redactEmail(recipient.email) instead of the raw address, matching the #1288 pattern used by the single-email worker. Reused the existing lib/logger/pii.ts redactEmail helper (no new helper added). The `to:` on the sendEmail() call itself keeps the raw address (required for delivery, not a log).
#1297 (telegram bot /info): removed the raw user email from the outbound Telegram reply — now shows 'Email: linked to your account'. Also defensively masked tenant billingEmail in the /pending admin listing via redactEmail(), since that also goes to Telegram servers.
#1295 (telegram fire-and-forget): sendReply() is now async and awaited at every call site; on !res.ok (e.g. 429 rate-limit) or a thrown/timeout error it logs via logError (level 'warning', context 'telegram-bot:sendReply') instead of swallowing. Each webhook branch sends at most one bounded (10s AbortSignal) reply then returns 200, so the webhook still responds promptly.
#1294 (stale WhatsApp token): in the lead-warming WhatsApp send, a !response.ok now detects a stale/expired access token (HTTP 401 or Meta OAuthException codes 190/102/463) and emits a clear structured logError (context 'worker:lead-warming:whatsapp:stale-token', tenantId + integrationId + status + metaErrorCode) telling the operator to re-connect WhatsApp, plus writes a 'WhatsApp token expired' errorMessage on the message row. No OAuth refresh flow exists; documented as a FOLLOW-UP in a code comment (automatic Meta token refresh/rotation is out of scope).
#1293 was intentionally SKIPPED because the issue is CLOSED (per orchestrator briefing and context).
Verification: npm run typecheck 0 errors; npm run lint 0 errors / 152 warnings (baseline unchanged, touched files added zero warnings); npm run test:unit 5389 passed / 327 files. No unit tests exist for worker.ts or the telegram route. Grep confirmed no raw email/token/secret appears in any log statement or Redis-persisted return value on the touched lines.
